announcements.title: Final Course Assessment is now open
announcements.body:
Hi everyone,

A quick supportive reminder: the Final Course Assessment is now available.

Open: Sunday, Aug 2

Due: Monday, Aug 3 at 11:59 PM

This is an individual assessment. It is open-note and open-book, and you may use course materials freely. Please do your own work — no collaboration with classmates or anyone else.

Before you start the Canvas quiz, review the question statements and complete your analysis first:

Fernbank Questions (data analytics)

Golf like a Pro (decision analytics)

Once you begin the quiz, you’ll have 24 hours in one sitting to enter your answers. The quiz still locks at the deadline even if time remains on the 24-hour clock, so plan a window that works for you.

You’ve put in strong work this term — trust your preparation, take it one question at a time, and do your best.

If you need help during the exam window, email me or we can set up a quick Zoom. I’m happy to support you.

Good luck,
Prof. Gu

announcements.title: Class 10 (7/30) Sensitivity, Value of Information, and Exam Review
announcements.body:
Today we wrapped up sensitivity analysis on decision problems, then introduced value of information and connected it to a practical pricing question: why a renowned consulting firm like BCG can charge a higher price than a small regional firm. The core idea is that better information can change decisions and create measurable value — and that value helps explain differences in what clients are willing to pay.

We also reviewed the overall course structure and the logistics for the final exam. Per our discussion, we will OPEN the final assessment at 12:00 AM on Sunday 8/2 and CLOSE at 11:59 PM on Monday 8/3. You will have access to the exam question statements without starting the exam:

Please let me know if there are any questions during the exam period.

Here is the course notes and recording for today.

Complete the course evaluation on Canvas before it closes. Your feedback is important as I continue to update and improve the course each year.

announcements.title: Class 9 (7/27) Sensitivity Analysis
announcements.body:
Today we introduced sensitivity analysis which explores the impact of inputs (Xs) on the outputs (y). To do so, we

first develop a spreadsheet model, which consists of Input->Model-> Output, to represent the decision making process and visualize the impact of input on outputs. (Note that everything needs to be linked together.)

Next, we employed Excel Data Table to visualize the impact of input X on output(s) over a range of values.

When working on the data table, trying to approach from the table perspective and think about the columns and rows structure. Specifically, we have 1) first column, 2) first row, 3) cells, and 4) top left corner. 

For ONE-var data table, we use the first row to represent the output(s)

For Two-var data table, we use the first row as 2nd input, and top-left corner as the output.

Finally, we introduced Excel Goal Seek to identify the break-even value that makes the top two alternatives yield the same expected value. 

Mathematically, we're finding the X value which makes y1=y2, or y1-y2 = 0

Note that for Excel Goal Seek,

The Set Cell must be a formula related to output 

the To Value Option must be a numerical value, not a formula. 

Here is the course notes and recording for today. 

Assignments after class:

Work on the Simulation on Excel Data Tables 

Work on break-even analysis for the Falafel case

Complete and submit Group BTG Sensitivity before next class. Complete BTG tree included in the assignment.

announcements.title: Class 8 (7/23) Decision Analysis in Excel
announcements.body:
Today we reviewed decision trees and discussed how to solve a tree. Specifically, we implemented the backwards deduction process and started from the end of the tree and traced back.

For the end node, we summarize all the cash flows along the way

For an event (chance) node, we calculate the expected value (weighted average)

For a decision node, we choose the best (either maximize or minimize)

Next, we worked on implementing Decision Analytics in Excel with the TreePlan add-in. We started by discussing the BTG case, and identified all the necessary components required for the case: the alternatives, the states of nature, and the outcomes. Next, we discussed how to (1) organize such information in Excel and (2) develop a decision tree with TreePlan. Finally, we worked on developing the Traynor Wharf branch of the BTG case.

Here is the course notes and recording for today.

Assignments after class:

Complete and submit Individual BTG Tree before next class (due Mon 7/27 before class).

Skim Noonan’s book on Decision analysis

Work on the Simulation on Excel Data Tables

announcements.title: Class 7 (7/20) Decision Basics
announcements.body:
Today we reviewed two regression methods, OLS (linear) regression and logistic regression. We compared their main differences and discussed how to evaluate prediction quality. For the logistic model, we also spent time on interpretation: coefficients act on the log-odds scale, and the odds ratio has a multiplicative relationship with the odds — a one-unit change in X multiplies the odds by the odds ratio (rather than adding a fixed amount, as in linear regression).

We also started our transition from Data analytics to Decision analytics. Specifically, we discussed the main components to look for in a decision context: 1) Decision and alternatives, 2) (Uncertain) Events and corresponding States of Nature, and 3) Outcomes. Next, we organized the information in a graphical tool called a decision tree. We worked on how to develop a tree forwards (from left to right); next class, we will study how to solve a tree backwards (from right to left).

Here is the course notes and recording for today. 

Assignments after class:

Complete and submit Decision Basics Quiz before next class.

Work on the Simulation on creating a decision tree

Read Bistro-To-Go case and attempt creating the decision tree manually

Install treeplan add-in before next class. Additional help on installing the software is provided here (follow Mac or Windows instructions for your OS).

announcements.title: Class 6 (7/16) Cases, Residual and Logistic Regression
announcements.body:
Today we tried the same model building process on several cases, baseball, pilgrim, and store24. Note that the purpose of building a model may not always be about making prediction, and sometimes our goal is actually to understand relationship in the right (multiple regression) context. Specifically, for the store24 case, our goal was to understand the impact of tenure on the profitability. At the end, we conduct a simple cost and benefits analysis of the incentive. Please complete this analysis by considering the benefits from both the crew and manager tenure and submit a presentation slide.

Next, we visited residual analytics to explore nonlinear patterns of quantitative X variables. We can do one of two things: 1) treat the X as a nominal if it takes a few values, and 2) introduce a quadratic form.

Finally, we introduced logistic regression, which can help us predict a binary categorical variable, such as Yes or No. We interpret the model fit as well as the the impact of individual variables. 

Here is the course notes and recording for today. 

Assignments after class:

Complete and submit Group Store24 Analysis assignment. Due before Tuesday EOD 7/21.

Install treeplan add-in before next class. Make sure we follow the installation instructions for your computer OS, Mac or Windows.

announcements.title: Class 5 (7/13) Categorical and model building
announcements.body:
Today we discussed collinearity in multiple regression and leveraged categorical variables that are not binary. For regression purpose in Excel, we need to transform the variable into dummy variables, the basic binary form. Note that Excel and JMP use different baseline group, specifically Excel uses a particular category such as Cape Cod as baseline, while JMP uses the average of all categories as the baseline.

Next, we summarized the model building process, which starts with descriptive analytics and ends with a final model that captures significant variables. Specifically, we introduced a backward deduction process to gradually exclude insignificant variables from the model until all variables are significant. 

Here is the course notes and recording for today.

announcements.title: Class 4 (7/09) Multiple Regression with Categorical Variables
announcements.body:
Today we continued to work on regression. 

We first worked on the application stage of regression which entails making predictions with simple regression model. 

Next, we introduced R2 and multiple regression. The implementation is very similar to that for simple regression. So is the interpretation, except for the key difference of "Controlling for other variables, or holding other variables constant....". This additional phrase is important as it helps us see the marginal effect of a factor on the target. 

Finally, we discussed a little bit of the dark side of multiple regression, collinearity. It refers to the correlation between two X factors which affect the evaluation of individual impact on the target variable Y. 

Here is the course notes and recording for today. 

Assignments after class:

announcements.title: Class 3 (7/6) Linear Regression for "how much"
announcements.body:
In class 3, we differentiated slope from correlation. While correlation mainly focused on the direction and strength of a relationship, slope focuses on the "how much". Specifically, "how much" would Y change if X increases by one unit, or the rise/run. Other than adding a trendlline in Excel to identify the trend line, we studied how to implement linear regression with Analysis ToolPak. From the regression results, we can not only identify the slope, but also the evidences for determining

whether a trend is significant or random (p-value),

the regression model for prediction (y = mx +b)

the accuracy of the prediction (St Error of regression) 

Next, we extended our discussion to a multiple regression, which considers multiple X variables. We can follow similar way to interpret the significance and the slope of a variable in multiple regression.

Here is the course notes and recording for today.

announcements.title: Class 2 (7/1) Graph and Describe Two Variables
announcements.body:
Today in class, we discussed how to describe One variable graphically and with SAS JMP. With that, we looked at the Pilgrim Bank case and examined two variables as an example, 9Profit and 9Online. Next, we implemented descriptive analytics for describing the correlation of Two Quantitative variables in Excel and JMP, both numerically (w. correlation coefficient r) and graphically (w. scatter plot). As well as the association between a Quantitative and categorical variable, numerically (w. difference in group means) and graphically (w. diamond graph). Such relationship serves as the foundation for prediction.

announcements.title: Class 1 (6/29) Describe One Variable Numerically and Graphically.
announcements.body:
It's a pleasure meeting everyone today. I'm hopeful that we will have a great time together exploring how to leverage data for decision making. 

Today in class, we reviewed topics from stats workshop, we implemented descriptive analytics for One variable in Excel with Analysis ToolPak, both numerically (w. Descriptive Statistics) and graphically (w. Histogram). Obtaining these summaries are important, yet our main focus is on how to interpret these evidence in the context to develop a compelling story from data. And we treat the numbers (expected) and graphs (actually observed) as two sources of evidence to verify the story.
